findings.title: Button will no longer be right-aligned in .small-action
findings.body: Adding `@include flexbox()` to `.small-action` makes it a flex container, but the action button still relies on `float: right` (line 309). Floats are ignored for direct children of a flex container, so the button will be placed in source order after the description instead of being pushed to the right edge. Use `margin-left: auto`, `order`, or another flex mechanism to position the button.

findings.title: Header right alignment lacks a fallback for the prefixed flex syntaxes
findings.body: `.d-header .panel` is now positioned with `margin-left: auto` inside `.d-header .contents`, and the previous float-based layout was removed. Auto-margin alignment is not supported by the old `-webkit-box`/`-moz-box` flex syntaxes emitted by the new mixins, and non-flex browsers have no fallback. In those environments the panel may not be pushed to the right, breaking the header layout.

findings.title: align-items mixin omits -moz-box-align and emits an invalid -ms property
findings.body: The `align-items` mixin outputs `-webkit-box-align`, `-webkit-align-items`, `-ms-flex-align`, and standard `align-items`, but it does not output `-moz-box-align`. Since `flexbox()`/`inline-flex()` emit `-moz-box`/`-moz-inline-box`, old Firefox layouts are being targeted, yet alignment will not apply there. The mixin also outputs `-ms-align-items`, which is not a valid property. This can break vertical alignment in header, small-action, and badge layouts in legacy Firefox.

findings.title: order mixin does not translate values for legacy ordinal groups
findings.body: `order()` passes the modern `order` value directly to `-webkit-box-ordinal-group` and `-moz-box-ordinal-group`. The old box syntax uses 1-based ordinal groups and does not have the same zero/negative semantics as modern flex `order`, so values such as `0` or `1` will not behave correctly in legacy WebKit/Firefox. If these prefixes are meant to be supported, the mixin should convert the value (commonly `$val + 1`) or avoid emitting legacy properties.
